name: Grover Cleveland
role: Governor of New York, then President of the United States
bio: Grover Cleveland, governor of New York and then the 22nd president of the United States, appeared in the Cow Boy mostly through national news and editorial comment. In September 1884 the paper printed Theodore Roosevelt's criticism of Governor Cleveland's veto of a tenure-of-office bill, and that November it reported his election as president. During 1885 the paper discussed his civil service policy, criticized his orders on the Winnebago and Crow Creek reservations as unjust to settlers, and covered his order for cattlemen to leave the Indian Territory within forty days. In 1886 it commented on his marriage, the question of Dakota Governor Pierce's removal, and a cattlemen's letter to him from the International Range Association.
